lead.headline: Max wins the rain-hit Singapore sprint and takes pole for tonight's Grand Prix
lead.short: After a 30-minute rain delay, Russell beat Verstappen off the line and then crashed out of the lead at the last corner of the first lap; Max held off Hamilton by 2.5 seconds, with Leclerc third, for his first win of any kind in Singapore. In qualifying he beat both Ferraris, Leclerc beside him and Hamilton third, with Antonelli fourth. The race starts at 17:30 IST.
more: Nine cars dropped out of the sprint, and the two McLarens collided on the last lap. Russell, sixth fastest, starts from the back for his engine change. Antonelli, fourth in the sprint, extended his championship lead.

why.text: Max has never won the Singapore Grand Prix; tonight he starts it from pole, a week after his first win of the year.

update.new: Verstappen won the sprint and took pole for the race.
update.front: Max on pole after a sprint win, on race day, leads the paper for this reader.

seconds.headline: Supreme Court, sitting on a Sunday, bars illegal detentions and orders Delhi's Metro and internet restored
seconds.byline: TIMES OF INDIA · SCROLL · NDTV · 10–11 OCT
seconds.short: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana held a special sitting after pleas that their 9 October order had been flouted: the Metro was disrupted, two big railway stations shut and people detained well beyond the prohibited area. They told the government to keep peaceful gatherers free, run the Metro normally, keep the internet on and let lawyers and journalists work, and issued notice on a contempt plea. A Delhi court freed CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on condition they keep the peace for a year; the INDIA bloc plans a bigger protest on Monday.

why.text: The court has put limits on how far the state can go to stop the protests, the day before a larger one.

update.new: The Supreme Court barred illegal detentions; the CJP leaders were released.
update.front: A special Sunday order from the Supreme Court on the protests is front-page news on its own.

facts.orders: no illegal detention, Metro and internet restored

seconds.headline: Diomande's first goal beats Villarreal 1–0, but Vinícius is sent off for pulling hair and may miss the Clásico
seconds.short: Yan Diomande scored after a VAR check in the second half. Vinícius came on in the 52nd minute and thought he had made it 2–0, but VAR found he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up: goal off, red card. He apologised to the team and fans. Violent conduct without injury carries a ban of one to three games, and Madrid play Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing next in the league.

why.text: Three points back from the break, and the Clásico now hangs on the length of a ban.

update.new: Madrid won 1–0; Vinícius was sent off.
update.front: Madrid's result and a red card that may cost Vinícius the Clásico are front-page news for this reader.

preview.text: Marina Bay is slow, bumpy and hot: braking, traction and rear grip out of tight corners decide it, overtaking is hard, so qualifying and the safety car matter. Mercedes call it a stronghold, but their Sepang upgrade made the car slower in low-speed corners, and Singapore is where they will find out why. Verstappen arrives from his first win of the year, his third straight top-two finish.

picks.says: Singapore's slow corners are the real test of whether Mercedes' upgrade misfired or Sepang's surface was to blame.

screen.title: Digger
screen.reason: Indian critics found Iñárritu's oil-rig satire bold and rewarding, British and American ones laboured and smug; nearly all say Cruise's self-mocking turn is the reason to go.

screen.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion
screen.reason: A satisfying close to the franchise: Devgn's silent Vijay and Jaideep Ahlawat's cop carry it, though critics differ on how much the slow first half and the courtroom twists cost it.

screen.title: Verity
screen.reason: Most critics found the Colleen Hoover thriller silly and unconvincing, wasting Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson; a few enjoyed it as knowing camp.

screen.title: Resident Evil
screen.reason: Zach Cregger's reboot is gory, fast and often funny, with Austin Abrams a likeable lead; its critics say the chaos outruns any real dread.

screen.title: Heart of the Beast
screen.reason: An old-fashioned man-and-dog survival story in Alaska, lifted by Brad Pitt and the dog; reviews run from deeply moving to serviceable.

screen.title: The Uprising
screen.reason: Andrew Garfield is committed and the battle scenes hit hard, but most critics found Paul Greengrass's Peasants' Revolt epic thin, grim and flat.
